title: Krull-Akizuki Noetherianity for intermediate rings
statement: Let R be a Noetherian domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] with fraction field K, let L/K be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let D be a ring with R ⊆ D ⊆ L. Then D is Noetherian.

proof.text: Transfer the domain structure from L to D using the injective algebra map. Finite dimensionality implies Algebra.IsAlgebraic K L; IsFractionRing.comap_isAlgebraic_iff clears denominators to obtain Algebra.IsAlgebraic R L, and Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_injective gives Algebra.IsAlgebraic R D. For a nonzero ideal I choose a nonzero a in I. Mathlib Ideal.comap_ne_bot_of_algebraic_mem gives I.comap(algebraMap R D) != bot, hence a nonzero x in R whose image belongs to I. Handle the zero ideal by Submodule.fg_bot.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.119.12 (Tag 00PG), proof: Lemma 10.30.8 gives a nonzero element of I intersect R; equivalently the minimal-polynomial argument

proof.text: Use Module.finBasis K L and Basis.equivFun, restricted to R, to embed D R-linearly into Fin (finrank K L) -> K. Let M be its range and e : D equiv_R M the resulting LinearEquiv.ofInjective. Apply lem-sc-finite-length-global-submodule to M and nonzero x, then Module.length_ne_top_iff and isFiniteLength_iff_isNoetherian_isArtinian give IsNoetherian R (M/xM). QuotSMulTop.congr transports this to D/xD. Put J = Ideal.span {algebraMap R D x} <= I. Show J.restrictScalars R = x smul top by the membership descriptions of a principal ideal and a pointwise scalar multiple. Quotient equivalences transport Noetherianity to D/J, and isNoetherian_of_tower R yields IsNoetherianRing (D/J). The image of I under the quotient map is therefore finitely generated. Its intersection with the quotient kernel is J, a principal ideal. Ideal.fg_of_fg_map_of_fg_inf_ker_of_surjective yields I.FG. Finally apply isNoetherianRing_iff_ideal_fg.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.119.12 (Tag 00PG), proof: I/xA is a submodule of A/xA; Lemma 10.119.11 gives finite length of A/xA; hence I is finitely generated
